title: Runtime reconciler for intermittent OOMs triggered by misaligned KV eviction and allocator fragmentation
creator: Noah Chen
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private reported short, unpredictable GPU OOM spikes that correlate with heavy prefix eviction workloads. Investigation shows a sequence where accelerated prefix eviction leaves behind stale KV handles and small fragmented arenas in the runtime allocator; under high concurrency these fragments prevent contiguous allocation for tensor arenas and lead to rapid OOMs. This ticket implements a runtime-level reconciler and conservative reclamation policy to prevent the pathological interaction between KV eviction and allocator fragmentation.
symptoms_and_scope: Observed in Hosted high-burst customers and Dedicated pools running mixed sequence-length traffic. Private deployment reports limited to older CUDA/drivers and kernels where page-alignment behavior differs. Symptoms: sudden single-tenant OOMs lasting 30-90s, GPU kernel failures, session eviction storms, and subsequent tenant cold-start latency spikes. A small subset (~6 customers) escalated with production impact during traffic bursts.
root_cause_analysis: Root cause is a race between the KV eviction path and the allocator's free list coalescer. When prefixes are aggressively evicted, KV handles are marked for deferred reclamation; under concurrent steady-state allocations the allocator retains many sub-allocations sized for earlier activity, causing fragmentation. The sum of small fragmented arenas can exceed the largest contiguous tensor allocation required by some model sequences. Additionally, a bug in the KV handle lifecycle left tombstone entries that prevented timely coalescing of neighboring free blocks. Combined, these lead to rapid failure to satisfy large allocation requests and GPU OOMs.
mitigation_so_far:
- Emergency livepatch (hosted only) that delays aggressive prefix eviction and forces synchronous tombstone cleanup for high-risk tenants.
- Temporary quota reductions and request hedging for impacted customers.
- Canary image with aggressive allocator compaction deployed to a small Dedicated pool.
- Private customer advises: upgraded CUDA drivers and a suggested runtime flag to enable conservative reclaiming.
proposed_fix: 1) Implement a runtime reconciler component that: validates KV handle checksums before reclaim, drains tombstones more deterministically, and signals the allocator when adjacent free blocks are eligible for coalescing. 2) Add backpressure: if contiguous free memory falls below a threshold, slow down KV eviction and reduce per-tenant prefetch/keepalive. 3) Extend telemetry: per-tenant fragmentation delta, tombstone age histogram, and allocator contiguous-free gauge. 4) Provide a configuration knob for Private deployments to preferentially enable synchronous reclaim. 5) Automated canary rollout + progressive ramp with automatic rollback on OOM regression.
test_plan: Unit tests for KV handle checksum path and tombstone lifecycle
Integration tests: synthetic workload that alternates long-prefix writes with rapid evictions and verifies allocator coalescing and no OOM
Load test on Dedicated canary cluster with production-like sequence-length distribution (100k requests/hour) for 48h
Private deployment test harness using GPU image versions 520.x and 535.x to validate driver-sensitive behavior
Chaos test: introduce delayed reclaim and verify graceful backpressure and request hedging behavior
Automated regression for previous OOM signatures via recorded traces
telemetry_and_success_criteria:
- 95% reduction in P95 tenant OOM frequency in canary (compare 7-day window pre/post).
- Contiguous-free memory gauge never dropping below 'safety_threshold' during synthetic bursts.
- Tombstone-age 95th percentile < 2s in steady state.
- No increase in tail latency >10% for normal requests.
- Green across canary for 72h before 50% rollout.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR to runtime/main behind feature-flag. 2) Deploy to Hosted canaries for 48h with strict monitoring. 3) Expand to Dedicated low-traffic pools (10% of Dedicated capacity) for 72h. 4) Offer Private customers opt-in images and recommended config flags; schedule full Private rollout for customers with driver >= 530. 5) Full enable if canary metrics meet success criteria; otherwise roll back.
rollback_plan: Revert feature-flag at runtime control plane. Emergency rollback playbook: drain affected worker pool, redeploy last stable image, and reinstate temporary prefix-eviction throttle. Notify SRE/CS and impacted customers per incident comms template.
risk_assessment: Medium-high: changes touch allocator and KV reclamation paths, which are sensitive. Mitigation: feature-flag gating, staged rollout, extensive test harness, and additional telemetry. Hotpatch for Hosted only initially.

2026-02-20 PR: Added checksum guard on KV handle release. Unit tests added. Still observing fragmentation on synthetic workload.
2026-02-28 PR: Implemented allocator signal API to request urgent coalescing; demo'ed to runtime team. Integration tests green locally.
2026-03-05 PR: Full reconciler implementation opened (PR #4876). Canary deploy in Hosted (2% traffic). Monitoring dashboard updated with fragmentation gauges.
2026-03-08 PR: Canary passed basic health but observed slight tail latency increase (~6%). Decided to extend observation window to 72h before Dedicated canary.
2026-03-12 PR: Engineering review complete. Preparing deployment runbook and CS messaging. Targeting Dedicated canary next.
Action items: update runtime docs for Private deployments, add a migration note for customers on older GPU drivers, and schedule a knowledge-share with SRE.
